title: OPTIMA: Design-Space Exploration of Discharge-Based In-SRAM Computing: Quantifying Energy-Accuracy Trade-offs
problem: Circuit nonlinearities and PVT variations pose major challenges in designing robust in-SRAM computing accelerators. These physical constraints make it difficult to achieve reliable computation while maintaining energy efficiency.
motivation: In-SRAM computing promises significant energy efficiency gains, but addressing design challenges is critical for practical accelerator deployment.
method: OPTIMA is a modeling framework that analyzes bitline discharge and power consumption in 6T-SRAM-based accelerators. It models in-SRAM multiplications with ~100x simulation speed-up and 0.88 mV RMS error, enabling fast design-space exploration of circuit configurations. The framework identifies limiting factors and optimizes configurations for energy-accuracy tradeoffs, applied to quantized DNNs for classification.
key_novelty: A modeling framework for efficient bitline discharge analysis in 6T-SRAM that enables rapid design-space exploration of in-SRAM computing accelerators.
contributions: OPTIMA modeling framework for analyzing bitline discharge and power consumption in 6T-SRAM-based accelerators
~100x simulation speed-up with 0.88 mV RMS modeling error for in-SRAM multiplications
Optimized multiplier design achieving 1.05 pJ energy per 4-bit operation
Demonstrated quantized DNN classification: 71.8% (ImageNet top-1), 90.4% (ImageNet top-5), 92.5% (CIFAR-10)
primary_theme: energy-efficient in-SRAM computing design through circuit modeling
